SGPT is an abbreviation of Serum Glutamate Pyruvate Transaminase, also referred to as Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). It is a liver-secreted enzyme. SGPT assists in breaking down proteins and plays a crucial role in fuelling the body with energy derived from food.

The TORCH Profile – 4 IgM is a diagnostic blood test used to detect recent or active infections that may pose risks during pregnancy. It screens for Toxoplasma IgM, Rubella IgM, Cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgM, and Herpes Simplex Virus type 2 (HSV-2) IgM antibodies. The presence of IgM antibodies indicates a recent infection, helping clinicians assess potential causes of infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, or congenital infections. Early identification through this profile supports timely medical intervention, monitoring, and appropriate treatment to reduce complications for both mother and fetus.
preparation: No special preparation is required for this test. Fasting is not necessary, and you may eat and drink normally unless advised otherwise by your doctor. Inform your healthcare provider about any medications, supplements, or recent vaccinations you are taking, as these may influence test results. If you are pregnant or suspect pregnancy, please notify the laboratory staff. The test requires a simple blood sample, typically drawn from a vein in the arm.
